findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine to reach a dish plate temperature of 150-154F after running several cycles. Inspector discussed proper heat sanitizing temperatures with the person in charge (PIC). The facility has been directed to utilize the triple sink for chemical sanitation until the machine’s heat boosters have been adjusted to reach a minimum plate temperature of 158F (FDA food codes allows for +/-2 instrument error). Inform the inspector if the machine has been adjusted prior to the follow up date.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A sanitizer bucket on the prep counter was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Sanitizer buckets were emptied and remade at the 3 compartment sink wall-mounted dispenser. Sanitizer buckets were then observed at 400ppm quat. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade periodically.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The kitchen restroom door is not self-closing. Add a self-closer to the restroom door.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 A toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer spray bottles observed with no measurable quat sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Sanitizer concentrate jug was replaced and spray bottles were remade. Sanitizer was observed at 200 ppm.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on the label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulk is not sealing the edge of the dish area drainboards to the wall. Reseal drainboards to the wall. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored over ready-to-eat foods (shredded cheese, tortillas, etc) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Storage rearranged to prevent potential cross contamination. Discussed storing eggs below ready-to-eat food.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available on file. CORRECTED- Inspector provided a printed copy of a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy to be posted or kept on file.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Spray bottles used for quat sanitizer were empty at the start of inspection. Breakfast service recently ended and lunch prep was underway. Solutions at proper concentration were provided during inspection. Ensure quat solutions are prepared and available for use during all hours of prep and operation.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Upon arrival a member of the kitchen staff was observed adjusting their face mask and did not wash hands prior to continuing with their next task. Handwashing between tasks and after adjustment of face mask were discussed. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for remainder of inspection. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Irreversible registering temperature indicator was not available for checking the final rinse surface temperature at the dishes during a ware washing cycle. Options for dish machine temperature test strips and maximum registering thermometers were discussed.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 After making a phone call an employee returned to the prep area and got a pair of gloves to finish prep without first washing hands. Hand washing between tasks and glove changes were discussed. Hands were washed prior to putting gloves to continue with salad bar prep.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed prior to donning gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee adjusted face mask with gloved hands while doing salad bar prep and did not immediately remove gloves for disposal. Proper glove use was discussed. Ensure gloves are changed between tasks/as needed and any time gloved hands touch general surfaces unrelated to food prep/handling.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.
